paper.title: Tighter Regret Lower Bound for Gaussian Process Bandits with Squared Exponential Kernel in Hypersphere

settings.name_in_paper: GP bandit problem on the hypersphere with the SE kernel (cumulative regret, frequentist)
unmapped: input domain is the hypersphere S^d = {x in R^{d+1}: ||x||_2 = 1} (d is the manifold dimension)
settings.definition_quote: In GP bandits, the underlying reward function $f: \mX \rightarrow \R$ is assumed to belong to $\mH_k(\mX)$ and to have bounded RKHS norm $\|f\|_{\mH_k(\mX)} \leq B < \infty$. ... the learner observes a noisy function value $y_t \coloneqq f(\bx_t) + \epsilon_t$, where $\epsilon_t \sim \mN(0, \sigma^2)$ ... minimize either the cumulative regret $R_T \coloneqq \sum_{t \in [T]} \rbr{\max_{\bx \in \mX} f(\bx) - f(\bx_t)}$

settings.name_in_paper: GP bandit problem on the hypersphere with the SE kernel (finding an epsilon-optimal point w.p. 1-delta)
unmapped: input domain is the hypersphere S^d in R^{d+1}
settings.definition_quote: the simple regret $r_T \coloneqq \max_{\bx \in \mX} f(\bx) - f(\hat{\bx}_T)$, where ... $\hat{\bx}_T \in \mX$ is the estimated maximizer reported by the algorithm at the end of step $T$.

settings.name_in_paper: GP bandit problem on the hypersphere with the SE kernel (expected simple regret)
unmapped: input domain is the hypersphere S^d in R^{d+1}
settings.definition_quote: suppose that there exists an algorithm that achieves $\Ep[r_T] \leq \epsilon$ for any $f \in \mH_k(\mX, B)$.

conditions: algorithm achieves r_T <= epsilon with probability at least 1-delta for any f in H_k(X,B)
d and theta_ls are fixed constants (hidden constants depend on them)
RKHS norm ||f|| <= B (B mapped to S)

source.label: thm:improved_sr_lower_bound
source.quote: Fix any $\delta \in (0, 1/3)$, $\epsilon \in (0, 1/2)$, $B > 0$, and $T \in \N_+$. Consider the GP bandit problem on $\mX = \mbS^d$ with the SE kernel ... suppose that there exists an algorithm that achieves $r_T \leq \epsilon$ with probability at least $1 - \delta$ for any $f \in \mH_k(\mX, B)$. Then, if $\epsilon/B$ is sufficiently small, it is necessary that $T = \Omega(\frac{\sigma^2}{\epsilon^2} (\ln \frac{B}{\epsilon})^{d} (\ln \ln \frac{B}{\epsilon})^{-d}\ln \frac{1}{\delta})$.

results.notes: Paper's B (RKHS norm bound) mapped to S. Lower bound on the number of steps needed to find an epsilon-optimal point with prob 1-delta.

bound.regime: sigma^2 ln(1/delta)/B^2 = O(T) with sufficiently small implied constant

conditions: for any algorithm there exists f in H_k(X,B) such that the bound holds with probability at least delta
sigma^2 ln(1/delta)/B^2 = O(T) with sufficiently small implied constant

source.label: thm:improved_cr_lower_bound
source.quote: Consider the same setting as in \thmref{thm:improved_sr_lower_bound}. Furthermore, assume $\sigma^2 (\ln (1/\delta))/B^2 = O(T)$ with a sufficiently small implied constant. Then, for any algorithm, there exists a function $f \in \mH_k(\mX, B)$ such that the following inequality holds with probability at least $\delta$: $R_T = \Omega(\sqrt{T \sigma^2 (\ln \frac{B^2 T}{\sigma^2 \ln \frac{1}{\delta}})^{d} (\ln \ln \frac{B^2 T}{\sigma^2 \ln \frac{1}{\delta}})^{-d} \ln \frac{1}{\delta}})$.

results.notes: Regret lower bound holding with probability at least delta (not 1-delta); recorded as high_probability_regret. B mapped to S.

conditions: algorithm achieves E[r_T] <= epsilon for any f in H_k(X,B)
SE kernel with lengthscale theta_ls; d and theta_ls fixed constants

source.label: cor:expected_sr_lower_bound
source.quote: Fix any $\epsilon \in (0, 1/12)$, $B > 0$, and $T \in \N_+$. ... suppose that there exists an algorithm that achieves $\Ep[r_T] \leq \epsilon$ for any $f \in \mH_k(\mX, B)$. Then, if $\epsilon/B$ is sufficiently small, it is necessary that $T = \Omega(\frac{\sigma^2}{\epsilon^2} (\ln \frac{B}{\epsilon})^{d} (\ln \ln \frac{B}{\epsilon})^{-d})$.

results.notes: Number of steps needed for expected simple regret <= epsilon.

bound.regime: sigma^2/B^2 = O(T) with sufficiently small implied constant

conditions: SE kernel with lengthscale theta_ls; d and theta_ls fixed constants
sigma^2/B^2 = O(T) with sufficiently small implied constant

source.label: cor:expected_cr_lower_bound
source.quote: Suppose that $d \in \N_+$ and $\theta > 0$ are fixed constants, and $B$, $\sigma^2 > 0$, and $T \in \N_+$ satisfy $\sigma^2/B^2 = O(T)$ with a sufficiently small implied constant. Then, for any algorithm, there exists a function $f \in \mH_k(\mX, B)$ such that ... $\Ep[R_T] = \Omega(\sqrt{T \sigma^2 (\ln \frac{B^2 T}{\sigma^2})^{d} (\ln \ln \frac{B^2 T}{\sigma^2})^{-d}})$.

results.notes: R_T defined through f values at queried points, so its expectation is pseudo-regret.

conditions: algorithm achieves r_T <= epsilon with probability at least 1-delta for any f in H_k(X,B)
SE kernel; d and theta_ls fixed constants

source.label: cor:org_lb_sr
source.quote: Simple regret lower bound on the hypersphere, extended from \citep{cai2021on} ... Then, if $\epsilon/B$ is sufficiently small, it is necessary that $T = \Omega(\frac{\sigma^2}{\epsilon^2} (\ln \frac{B}{\epsilon})^{d/2} \ln \frac{1}{\delta})$.

results.notes: Extension of Cai & Scarlett's [0,1]^d result to the hypersphere, proved in Appendix A for completeness; superseded by Theorem 3.1.

conditions: for any algorithm there exists f in H_k(X,B) such that the bound holds with probability at least delta

source.label: cor:org_lb_cr
source.quote: Consider the same setting as in \corref{cor:org_lb_sr}. Furthermore, assume $\sigma^2 (\ln (1/\delta))/B^2 = O(T)$ with a sufficiently small implied constant. Then, for any algorithm, there exists a function $f \in \mH_k(\mX, B)$ such that the following inequality holds with probability at least $\delta$: $R_T = \Omega(\sqrt{T \sigma^2 (\ln \frac{B^2 T}{\sigma^2 \ln \frac{1}{\delta}})^{d/2}})$.

results.notes: Extension of Cai & Scarlett to hypersphere; superseded by Theorem 3.2. Theorem 5.1 (MIG bound gamma_T = O((ln T)^{d+1}(ln ln T)^{-d})) not recorded as it is not a regret guarantee.
